summary: Backend testing for Dubita (Italian video dubbing). 11/13 pytest cases pass. Auth, voices, project CRUD, user isolation and error handling work correctly. The dubbing pipeline is BROKEN at two stages: (1) YouTube download fails with HTTP 403 Forbidden due to YouTube bot detection from this cloud IP, and (2) the GPT translation step uses an invalid model name 'gpt-5.4'. Whisper transcription was also broken (dict vs attribute access) but I patched it to unblock further testing.

critical.issue: yt-dlp returns HTTP 403 Forbidden for ALL YouTube videos (tested with jNQXAC9IVRw 'Me at the zoo'). YouTube bot-detects the cloud IP. Multiple player_client extractor args attempted (default android_vr, web_safari, ios) - all return 403 or 'Sign in to confirm you're not a bot'. Pipeline immediately fails at progress=5 with status=error and never gets past the download stage. Also: PRE-fix - yt-dlp binary was not on the backend supervisor's PATH (PATH stripped to /usr/local/sbin:/usr/local/bin:...). I added a symlink at /usr/local/bin/yt-dlp -> /root/.venv/bin/yt-dlp to make it resolvable, but the 403 is the real blocker.

dubbing.py line 129 uses .with_model('openai', 'gpt-5.4') which is rejected by emergent proxy / litellm: BadRequestError 'Invalid model name passed in model=gpt-5.4'. Pipeline progresses through download (skipped for upload), audio extract, Whisper transcription (succeeds with 3 segments), then aborts at progress=60 in translate_segments_to_italian(). Use a real model name e.g. 'gpt-4o-mini' or 'gpt-4o'.

Original code accessed Whisper response segments as objects (s.start, s.end, s.text) but emergentintegrations + litellm return them as DICTS. Caused 'dict object has no attribute start' and aborted pipeline at progress=35. I patched dubbing.py to handle both dict and object cases. Verified Whisper now correctly returns 3 segments for the sample mp4. This is a code bug - please review the patch.

Backend supervisor process PATH does NOT include /root/.venv/bin, so any binary installed only inside the venv (yt-dlp) is unreachable. Fix permanently by either (a) adding 'environment=PATH="/root/.venv/bin:..."' to supervisor backend block, or (b) keeping the /usr/local/bin symlink I created. Currently mitigated via symlink.

minor.issue: List endpoint strips 'segments' for lightweight response (good), but the detail endpoint returns full doc including raw MongoDB _id is correctly popped. No issue, just confirming.

action_items: FIX (CRITICAL): Replace .with_model('openai', 'gpt-5.4') in /app/backend/dubbing.py line 129 with a valid model such as 'gpt-4o-mini' or 'gpt-4o'. gpt-5.4 does not exist.

FIX (CRITICAL): YouTube download path is unusable - HTTP 403 from this cloud IP. Options: (a) add cookies/PO token support via --cookies-from-browser, (b) use a different YouTube extractor strategy, (c) require user-supplied cookies, or (d) document YouTube as 'best-effort' and emphasize file upload. Consider adding --extractor-args with PO token if available.
FIX (DEPLOY): Make yt-dlp permanently reachable by the backend - add PATH to supervisor backend program block. I created a symlink at /usr/local/bin/yt-dlp as a temporary fix.

REVIEW: The Whisper segments dict-vs-attribute patch I applied to /app/backend/dubbing.py (transcribe_audio function). Confirms Whisper returns dicts via emergentintegrations + litellm; please code-review.
RETEST: After GPT model fix, re-run /app/backend/tests/test_upload_pipeline.py to verify end-to-end pipeline (Whisper -> translate -> TTS -> mux) and dubbed video download works.
critical_code_review_comments: dubbing.py uses 'gpt-5.4' which is not a real OpenAI model name. Use gpt-4o-mini / gpt-4o.
dubbing.py:transcribe_audio() assumed objects for litellm Whisper segments - they are dicts. (patched)
auth.py uses datetime.timezone.utc and bcrypt correctly. JWT cookie sets samesite='none' + secure=True which is correct for cross-site cookie use. httpOnly cookie is set.
seed_admin() correctly updates password when env ADMIN_PASSWORD changes (matches integration_playbook). Idempotent.
No brute-force / rate-limit on /api/auth/login (auth playbook recommends lockout after 5 failed attempts). Not blocking but worth adding.
/api/projects/upload allows arbitrary file size (no max-size guard). Could be DoS vector. MAX_DURATION_SEC=1800 is enforced on the decoded video duration but the upload itself isn't capped.
server.py CORS allow_origins=[FRONTEND_URL, 'http://localhost:3000'] - good, no wildcard with credentials.
Background task runs the pipeline inside the request worker process; long pipelines may be killed on backend restart. Consider a worker queue (RQ/Celery) for production.

context_for_next_testing_agent: 1) Auth/voices/projects-CRUD endpoints are all green. 2) The YouTube pipeline cannot be tested in this env due to YouTube blocking the cloud IP with HTTP 403 - retest only if cookies/PO token are configured. 3) Upload pipeline test (/app/backend/tests/test_upload_pipeline.py) is the easiest end-to-end smoke - it uses /tmp/test_sample.mp4 which you may need to regenerate via /tmp/make_mp4.py if /tmp was cleared. 4) The Whisper-segments-as-dicts patch is applied; the next blocker once GPT model is fixed will likely be translate->TTS->mux which I haven't been able to validate yet. Poll status with timeout 6 min and look for status=done + progress=100 + segments[*].text_it populated + dubbed_video_path set.
rca_of_the_issue: Issue 1 (YouTube 403): YouTube's anti-bot system returns 403 to cloud datacenter IPs without a logged-in session / PO token. Reproduce: 'yt-dlp -f best https://www.youtube.com/watch?v=jNQXAC9IVRw' fails identically from CLI. Mitigation requires --cookies-from-browser=chrome (not feasible headless) or supplying user-provided cookies, or YouTube PO token via --extractor-args 'youtube:po_token=...'. Issue 2 (gpt-5.4): String literal 'gpt-5.4' in dubbing.py line 129 is not an OpenAI model. The emergent proxy returns 400 BadRequest. Fix: replace with 'gpt-4o-mini'. Issue 3 (Whisper segments): emergentintegrations -> litellm.atranscription with verbose_json returns TranscriptionResponse where .segments is list[dict] not list[Segment]; original code used attribute access. Fix: dict-aware access (already patched). Issue 4 (yt-dlp PATH): supervisor strips PATH to system default; yt-dlp lived only in /root/.venv/bin. Symlinked to /usr/local/bin/yt-dlp.
